meta.title: USCIS 2025 Civics Test — 128 Questions
meta.source: USCIS 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), M-1778 (09/25)
meta.studyGuide: One Nation, One People: The USCIS 2025 Civics Test Study Guide (M-1175)

special6520.eligibility: Age 65+ and lawful permanent resident 20+ years; may study only starred questions and test in their chosen language.

notes: Distractors (wrong answers) are authored for MCQ use and are NOT official USCIS content.
The real USCIS test is oral and free-recall; MCQ is a study aid.
answerType 'volatile' answers come from remote config (uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates).
answerType 'variesByState' answers come from a per-state dataset set by the user's state.
Some questions have multiple official correct answers; serve one as correct and draw wrong options from 'distractors'.

questions.question: What is the form of government of the United States?
questions.explanation: The U.S. is a republic where citizens elect representatives; power is defined and limited by the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the supreme law of the land?
questions.explanation: The Constitution is the highest law; all other laws must agree with it.

questions.question: Name one thing the U.S. Constitution does.
correctAnswers: Protects the rights of the people
questions.explanation: The Constitution sets up the government, defines its powers and parts, and protects people's rights.

questions.question: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words “We the People.” What does “We the People” mean?
distractors: Power belongs only to the states
Only people born here have rights
questions.explanation: “We the People” expresses self-government: the people, not a king, hold power.

questions.question: How are changes made to the U.S. Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution is changed through amendments.

questions.question: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
correctAnswers: (The basic) rights of people living in the United States
distractors: The right of states to secede
questions.explanation: The Bill of Rights (first 10 amendments) protects basic individual rights.

questions.question: How many amendments does the U.S. Constitution have?
questions.explanation: There are 27 amendments to the Constitution.

questions.question: Why is the Declaration of Independence important?
correctAnswers: It says America is free from British control.
It says all people are created equal.
distractors: It sets up the three branches of government.
It is the supreme law of the land.
It created the Bill of Rights.
questions.explanation: The Declaration announced independence and stated that all people have inherent rights.

questions.question: What founding document said the American colonies were free from Britain?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Independence (1776) announced freedom from Britain.

questions.question: Name two important ideas from the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution.
questions.explanation: Core ideas include equality, liberty, natural rights, and limited, self-government.

questions.question: The words “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness” are in what founding document?
questions.explanation: That phrase appears in the Declaration of Independence.

questions.question: What is the economic system of the United States?
questions.explanation: The U.S. has a capitalist, free-market economy.

questions.question: What is the rule of law?
correctAnswers: No one is above the law.
distractors: The President can change any law.
Only citizens must follow the law.
questions.explanation: Rule of law means everyone — including leaders and government — must follow the law.

questions.question: Many documents influenced the U.S. Constitution. Name one.
questions.explanation: Several earlier documents, like the Articles of Confederation and Federalist Papers, influenced the Constitution.

questions.question: There are three branches of government. Why?
correctAnswers: So one part does not become too powerful
distractors: To give the President more power
To divide the country into regions
questions.explanation: Three branches separate power so no single branch becomes too powerful.

questions.question: Name the three branches of government.
questions.explanation: The three branches are legislative (Congress), executive (President), and judicial (courts).

questions.question: The President of the United States is in charge of which branch of government?
questions.explanation: The President leads the executive branch.

questions.question: What part of the federal government writes laws?
questions.explanation: Congress — the legislative branch — writes federal laws.

questions.question: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
distractors: The Senate and the Supreme Court
The President and the Vice President
questions.explanation: Congress has two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.question: Name one power of the U.S. Congress.
questions.explanation: Congress writes laws, declares war, and makes the federal budget.

questions.question: How many U.S. senators are there?
questions.explanation: There are 100 senators — two from each of the 50 states.

questions.question: How long is a term for a U.S. senator?
questions.explanation: A U.S. senator serves a 6-year term.

questions.question: Who is one of your state’s U.S. senators now?
questions.explanation: Answer with a current U.S. senator from your state. (D.C. and territory residents have no U.S. senators.)

questions.question: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: The House has 435 voting members.

questions.question: How long is a term for a member of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: A House member serves a 2-year term.

questions.question: Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators?
correctAnswers: To more closely follow public opinion
distractors: Because there are more of them
Because they are limited to one term
So they can become senators faster
questions.explanation: Shorter terms keep representatives closely tied to public opinion.

questions.question: How many senators does each state have?
questions.explanation: Each state has exactly two senators.

questions.question: Why does each state have two senators?
distractors: To match the number of branches
Because of the Bill of Rights
questions.explanation: Two senators per state gives every state equal representation — the Great Compromise.

questions.question: Name your U.S. representative.
questions.explanation: Answer with your current U.S. representative. (Territory residents may name their Delegate/Commissioner or state they have no voting representative.)

questions.question: What is the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives now?
questions.explanation: This answer changes. Use the current Speaker as listed at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

questions.question: Who does a U.S. senator represent?
questions.explanation: A senator represents all the people of their state.

questions.question: Who elects U.S. senators?
questions.explanation: Citizens of each state elect their senators (since the 17th Amendment).

questions.question: Who does a member of the House of Representatives represent?
questions.explanation: A representative represents the people of their congressional district.

questions.question: Who elects members of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Citizens of each congressional district elect their representative.

questions.question: Some states have more representatives than other states. Why?
questions.explanation: House seats are based on state population, so more populous states have more representatives.

questions.question: The President of the United States is elected for how many years?
questions.explanation: A President is elected to a 4-year term.

questions.question: The President of the United States can serve only two terms. Why?
correctAnswers: To keep the president from becoming too powerful
distractors: Because of the Bill of Rights
questions.explanation: The 22nd Amendment limits a President to two terms.

questions.question: What is the name of the President of the United States now?
questions.explanation: This answer changes with elections. Use the current President as listed at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

questions.question: What is the name of the Vice President of the United States now?
questions.explanation: This answer changes with elections. Use the current Vice President as listed at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

questions.question: If the president can no longer serve, who becomes president?
correctAnswers: The Vice President (of the United States)
questions.explanation: The Vice President becomes President if the President cannot serve.

questions.question: Name one power of the president.
questions.explanation: The President signs or vetoes bills, enforces laws, leads the military, and appoints judges.

questions.question: Who is Commander in Chief of the U.S. military?
distractors: The Chairman of the Joint Chiefs
questions.explanation: The President is Commander in Chief of the military.

questions.question: Who signs bills to become laws?
questions.explanation: The President signs bills into law.

questions.question: Who vetoes bills?
questions.explanation: The President can veto (reject) bills passed by Congress.

questions.question: Who appoints federal judges?
questions.explanation: The President appoints federal judges (the Senate confirms them).

questions.question: The executive branch has many parts. Name one.
questions.explanation: The executive branch includes the President, the Cabinet, and federal departments and agencies.

questions.question: What does the President’s Cabinet do?
correctAnswers: Advises the President (of the United States)
questions.explanation: The Cabinet advises the President.

questions.question: What are two Cabinet-level positions?
correctAnswers: Secretary of Health and Human Services
Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
Administrator of the Small Business Administration
Director of the Central Intelligence Agency
Director of the Office of Management and Budget
distractors: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Cabinet-level positions include the Attorney General and the various Secretaries; the Speaker, Chief Justice, and governors are not Cabinet members.

questions.question: Why is the Electoral College important?
correctAnswers: It decides who is elected president.
It provides a compromise between the popular election of the president and congressional selection.
distractors: It counts the population every ten years.
questions.explanation: The Electoral College decides who becomes President.

questions.question: What is one part of the judicial branch?
questions.explanation: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

questions.question: What does the judicial branch do?
correctAnswers: Decides if a law goes against the (U.S.) Constitution
questions.explanation: The judicial branch reviews and explains laws and decides if they violate the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the highest court in the United States?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country.

questions.question: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has nine seats.

questions.question: How many Supreme Court justices are usually needed to decide a case?
questions.explanation: A simple majority — five of nine — is usually needed to decide a case.

questions.question: How long do Supreme Court justices serve?
distractors: Until the next president is elected
questions.explanation: Supreme Court justices serve for life (a lifetime appointment).

questions.question: Supreme Court justices serve for life. Why?
distractors: Because they are elected for life
To keep them loyal to the President
Because the Constitution requires nine judges
questions.explanation: Life terms keep justices independent of political pressure.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Justice of the United States now?
questions.explanation: This answer can change. Use the current Chief Justice as listed at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

questions.question: Name one power that is only for the federal government.
questions.explanation: Only the federal government can print money, declare war, make treaties, and set foreign policy.

questions.question: Name one power that is only for the states.
questions.explanation: States handle things like schools, police, fire departments, driver's licenses, and zoning.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 10th Amendment?
correctAnswers: (It states that the) powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people.
distractors: It gives women the right to vote.
questions.explanation: The 10th Amendment reserves powers not given to the federal government to the states or the people.

questions.question: Who is the governor of your state now?
questions.explanation: Answer with your state's current governor. (D.C. residents answer that D.C. has no governor.) This changes with elections.

questions.question: What is the capital of your state?
questions.explanation: Answer with your state's capital. Distractors can be other states' capitals. (D.C. is not a state; territory residents name the territory's capital.)

questions.question: There are four amendments to the U.S. Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.
correctAnswers: You don’t have to pay (a poll tax) to vote.
Any citizen can vote. (Women and men can vote.)
A male citizen of any race (can vote).
distractors: You must pass a test to vote.
questions.explanation: Voting amendments extended the vote regardless of race or sex, ended poll taxes, and set the voting age at 18.

questions.question: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?
questions.explanation: Only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury.

questions.question: What are three rights of everyone living in the United States?
distractors: The right to vote in federal elections
The right to a government job
The right to run for president
questions.explanation: Everyone in the U.S. has freedoms like speech, religion, assembly, and petition; voting and running for office are limited to citizens.

questions.question: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
questions.explanation: The Pledge shows loyalty to the United States and its flag.

questions.question: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.
correctAnswers: Give up loyalty to other countries
Obey the laws of the United States
Serve (help, do important work for) the nation (if needed)
Be loyal to the United States
questions.explanation: New citizens promise to give up foreign loyalties, defend the Constitution, obey the laws, and serve if needed.

questions.question: How can people become United States citizens?
correctAnswers: Be born in the United States, under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment
Derive citizenship (under conditions set by Congress)
distractors: By living here five years automatically
questions.explanation: Citizenship comes by birth (14th Amendment), naturalization, or derivation set by Congress.

questions.question: What are two examples of civic participation in the United States?
correctAnswers: Give an elected official your opinion (on an issue)
Support or oppose an issue or policy
questions.explanation: Civic participation includes voting, campaigning, joining groups, and contacting officials.

questions.question: What is one way Americans can serve their country?
correctAnswers: Work for local, state, or federal government
questions.explanation: Americans can serve by voting, paying taxes, obeying the law, or serving in government or the military.

questions.question: Why is it important to pay federal taxes?
correctAnswers: All people pay to fund the federal government
distractors: So you can run for office
questions.explanation: Paying federal taxes is required by law and funds the federal government.

questions.question: It is important for all men age 18 through 25 to register for the Selective Service. Name one reason why.
correctAnswers: Makes the draft fair, if needed
questions.explanation: Registering for the Selective Service is required by law and keeps a possible draft fair.

questions.question: The colonists came to America for many reasons. Name one.
distractors: To find gold only for Britain
questions.explanation: Colonists came for freedom, religious liberty, economic opportunity, and to escape persecution.

questions.question: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
questions.explanation: American Indians (Native Americans) lived here before Europeans arrived.

questions.question: What group of people was taken and sold as slaves?
questions.explanation: Africans were taken and sold as slaves.

questions.question: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: The American Revolution (Revolutionary War) won independence from Britain.

questions.question: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain.
correctAnswers: British soldiers stayed in Americans’ houses (boarding, quartering)
distractors: To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: Reasons included high taxes, taxation without representation, quartering of soldiers, and no self-government.

questions.question: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Thomas Jefferson was the main writer of the Declaration of Independence.

questions.question: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

questions.question: The American Revolution had many important events. Name one.
correctAnswers: Washington Crossing the Delaware (Battle of Trenton)
questions.explanation: Key Revolution events include Bunker Hill, Saratoga, Valley Forge, and Yorktown.

questions.question: There were 13 original states. Name five.
questions.explanation: The 13 original states ran along the Atlantic coast; states like Vermont, Ohio, and California joined later.

questions.question: What founding document was written in 1787?
questions.explanation: The U.S. Constitution was written in 1787.

questions.question: The Federalist Papers supported the passage of the U.S. Constitution. Name one of the writers.
questions.explanation: The Federalist Papers were written by Madison, Hamilton, and Jay (under the name Publius).

questions.question: Why were the Federalist Papers important?
correctAnswers: They helped people understand the (U.S.) Constitution.
distractors: They created the Bill of Rights.
questions.explanation: The Federalist Papers explained the Constitution and urged its ratification.

questions.question: Benjamin Franklin is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: Founded the first free public libraries
First Postmaster General of the United States
Helped write the Declaration of Independence
distractors: First President of the United States
Third President of the United States
questions.explanation: Franklin was a diplomat and inventor, the first Postmaster General, and helped write the Declaration.

questions.question: George Washington is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: First president of the United States
questions.explanation: Washington led the Continental Army and became the first President — the “Father of Our Country.”

questions.question: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: Writer of the Declaration of Independence
Third president of the United States
Doubled the size of the United States (Louisiana Purchase)
Writer of the Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom
distractors: Led troops in the Civil War
questions.explanation: Jefferson wrote the Declaration, was the third President, and made the Louisiana Purchase.

questions.question: James Madison is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: Fourth president of the United States
One of the writers of the Federalist Papers
questions.explanation: Madison is the “Father of the Constitution,” the fourth President, and a Federalist Papers author.

questions.question: Alexander Hamilton is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: One of the writers of the Federalist Papers
Helped establish the First Bank of the United States
distractors: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Hamilton was the first Secretary of the Treasury and a Federalist Papers author — he was never President.

questions.question: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?
questions.explanation: The U.S. bought the Louisiana Territory from France in 1803 (Alaska was later, from Russia).

questions.question: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s.
questions.explanation: 1800s wars include the War of 1812, the Mexican-American War, the Civil War, and the Spanish-American War.

questions.question: Name the U.S. war between the North and the South.
questions.explanation: The Civil War was fought between the North and the South.

questions.question: The Civil War had many important events. Name one.
questions.explanation: Civil War events include Fort Sumter, Gettysburg, Antietam, and the surrender at Appomattox.

questions.question: Abraham Lincoln is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: Led the United States during the Civil War
distractors: Doubled the size of the country
questions.explanation: Lincoln, the 16th President, led the Union in the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

questions.question: What did the Emancipation Proclamation do?
correctAnswers: Freed slaves in the Confederate states
Freed slaves in most Southern states
distractors: Gave women the right to vote
questions.explanation: The Emancipation Proclamation freed the slaves in the Confederate states.

questions.question: What U.S. war ended slavery?
questions.explanation: The Civil War ended slavery in the United States.

questions.question: What amendment says all persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are U.S. citizens?
questions.explanation: The 14th Amendment defines citizenship for those born or naturalized in the U.S.

questions.question: When did all men get the right to vote?
questions.explanation: The 15th Amendment (1870) gave all men the right to vote regardless of race.

questions.question: Name one leader of the women’s rights movement in the 1800s.
questions.explanation: 1800s women's rights leaders include Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
questions.explanation: 1900s wars include World War I, World War II, Korea, Vietnam, and the Persian Gulf War.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Why did the United States enter World War I?
correctAnswers: To support the Allied Powers (England, France, Italy, and Russia)
To oppose the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire, and Bulgaria)
distractors: To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: The U.S. entered WWI after Germany attacked U.S. ships, siding with the Allies.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: When did all women get the right to vote?
questions.explanation: The 19th Amendment (1920) gave all women the right to vote.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: What was the Great Depression?
correctAnswers: Longest economic recession in modern history
distractors: A period of rapid economic growth
questions.explanation: The Great Depression was the longest economic recession in modern history.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: When did the Great Depression start?
questions.explanation: The Great Depression began with the stock market crash of 1929.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Who was president during the Great Depression and World War II?
questions.explanation: Franklin Roosevelt was President during the Great Depression and most of World War II.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Why did the United States enter World War II?
correctAnswers: To support the Allied Powers (England, France, and Russia)
To oppose the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, and Japan)
distractors: Germany attacked U.S. ships in World War I
questions.explanation: The U.S. entered WWII after Japan bombed Pearl Harbor.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Dwight Eisenhower is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: President at the end of (during) the Korean War
Signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 (Created the Interstate System)
distractors: Led troops in the Civil War
questions.explanation: Eisenhower was a WWII general and the 34th President who created the Interstate Highway System.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Who was the United States’ main rival during the Cold War?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union (USSR) was the main U.S. rival during the Cold War.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: During the Cold War, what was one main concern of the United States?
questions.explanation: During the Cold War the U.S. was concerned about communism and nuclear war.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?
correctAnswers: To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: The U.S. entered the Korean War to stop the spread of communism.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Why did the United States enter the Vietnam War?
correctAnswers: To stop the spread of communism
distractors: To force Iraq out of Kuwait
questions.explanation: The U.S. entered the Vietnam War to stop the spread of communism.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: What did the civil rights movement do?
distractors: Gave women the right to vote
questions.explanation: The civil rights movement fought to end racial discrimination.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Martin Luther King, Jr. is famous for many things. Name one.
correctAnswers: Worked for equality for all Americans
Worked to ensure that people would “not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character”
distractors: Was the first African American president
questions.explanation: Dr. King was a leader of the civil rights movement who worked for equality.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?
correctAnswers: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
distractors: To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: The U.S. entered the Persian Gulf War to force the Iraqi military out of Kuwait.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: What major event happened on September 11, 2001 in the United States?
correctAnswers: Terrorists took over two planes and crashed them into the World Trade Center in New York City
Terrorists took over a plane and crashed into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia
Terrorists took over a plane originally aimed at Washington, D.C., and crashed in a field in Pennsylvania
distractors: The United States entered World War II
questions.explanation: On September 11, 2001, terrorists attacked the U.S., including the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Name one U.S. military conflict after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
questions.explanation: After 9/11 the U.S. fought the War on Terror, including wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Name one American Indian tribe in the United States.
questions.explanation: U.S. tribes include the Cherokee, Navajo, and Sioux; the Aztec, Maya, and Inca are not U.S. tribes.

questions.subcategory: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
questions.question: Name one example of an American innovation.
questions.explanation: American innovations include the light bulb, airplane, assembly line, and the moon landing.

questions.question: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.explanation: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States.

questions.question: Where is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor on Liberty Island.

questions.question: Why does the flag have 13 stripes?
correctAnswers: (Because the stripes) represent the original colonies
questions.explanation: The 13 stripes represent the 13 original colonies.

questions.question: Why does the flag have 50 stars?
correctAnswers: (Because there is) one star for each state
questions.explanation: The 50 stars represent the 50 states.

questions.question: What is the name of the national anthem?
questions.explanation: The national anthem is “The Star-Spangled Banner.”

questions.question: The Nation’s first motto was “E Pluribus Unum.” What does that mean?
questions.explanation: “E Pluribus Unum” means “out of many, one.”

questions.question: What is Independence Day?
correctAnswers: A holiday to celebrate U.S. independence (from Britain)
distractors: A holiday to honor soldiers who died
A holiday to honor all veterans
The day the Constitution was signed
questions.explanation: Independence Day (July 4) celebrates U.S. independence from Britain.

questions.question: Name three national U.S. holidays.
questions.explanation: National holidays include New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas.

questions.question: What is Memorial Day?
correctAnswers: A holiday to honor soldiers who died in military service
distractors: A holiday to honor all living veterans
questions.explanation: Memorial Day honors soldiers who died in military service.

questions.question: What is Veterans Day?
correctAnswers: A holiday to honor people in the (U.S.) military
A holiday to honor people who have served (in the U.S. military)
distractors: A holiday to honor soldiers who died in war
A holiday to honor the flag
questions.explanation: Veterans Day honors all people who have served in the U.S. military.
